description: Compiler-style product specification pipeline. E1 establishes the module contract; E2 creates and human-approves the permanent business journeys.
principles: Every completed step writes a permanent L4 artifact.
Pipeline state on disk is the resume authority; task payloads are orchestration only.
An existing module is resumable only when its pipeline declares flowId agentNewSolution4.
A foreign existing module is never overwritten and produces a visible collision error.
The /fast flag accepts the clarification defaults without requiring the widget to render.
Prompts live in the owning step folder; deterministic validation decides whether artifacts are trusted.

invocation.resumeRule: If l4/<module>/pipeline/pipeline.json belongs to agentNewSolution4, resume its next incomplete step. An approved E1 starts or resumes E2; an approved E2 reports E3 as the next unimplemented step. A module without the v4 pipeline marker is a collision.

steps.goal: Clarify the module name, actors, goal, boundaries and product languages, then write the initial permanent module contract.

checks: one or more unique normalized BCP-47 product languages
specStatus marks E1 approved and E2 as next
pipeline marks E1 approved only after module.defs.ts is written

steps.resume: A running E1 pipeline may be safely rerun. An approved E1 with module.defs.ts advances to e2-journeys when that step exists.
runtimeNotes: The root is a deterministic bootstrap and schedules a dedicated E1 clarification agent step; the root never owns a clarification payload.
In /fast, the E1 child afterPromptStep persists the defaults directly and completes without rendering the widget.
In interactive mode, the E1 child owns the standard clarification widget; its callback persists the artifacts and records a completed e1-result step.

steps.goal: Define the permanent business journeys, including entry policy and named business context, then freeze the human-approved business blocks with SHA-256 hashes.

checkpoint.approvalRule: Permanent journey files are written only after approval. A change request starts another E2 generation round and returns to this widget.

checks: unique stable journey, step, context, rule and feature ids
entry mode is coldStart, contextRequired, contextOrLookup or eventDriven
required context is carried, supplied by a prerequisite, or produced by an earlier step
act and decide steps cannot operate on an existing record without prior context
prerequisite journey references exist and do not reference themselves
every now feature references at least one journey step

steps.resume: A running or waiting-human E2 reopens generation/review. An approved E2 advances to e3-ontology.
runtimeNotes: The root uses a deterministic bootstrap and schedules an E2 agent step.
The model proposes a review bundle; the deterministic gate runs before the widget opens.
The widget displays prerequisites, entry context, context flow, rules, features and outcomes.
Duplicate approve/change events are ignored by a single-submit guard.
In /fast the valid E2 proposal is approved without rendering the widget.
